title: Real Talk From Publishers: What We’re Hearing at DV's News Accelerator Forums
summary: In DV News Accelerator™ forums in New York City and London, news publishers spoke candidly about industry trends including AI, brand suitability and more.
body_markdown:
**By Jack Marshall, Head of News, Policy and Content Partnerships**


DV actively encourages greater advertiser investment in news. In the two years since we established the DV News Accelerator™ program, we’ve worked closely with news publishers to understand how we can best support their monetization needs.


As part of this initiative, this year we brought together leaders from major news publishers for a series of forums in New York City and London. The sessions included candid, constructive discussions about the challenges and opportunities publishers are seeing in the market, and some recurring themes and topics emerged. Here’s a look at what’s on news publishers’ minds:


## 1. It’s Time for Ad Spend to Catch Up With the Research


A growing body of evidence highlights the persuasive power of news and the value it brings to advertisers. Ads in professionally produced news content consistently


[outperform](https://doubleverify.com/blog/web/publisher/advertising-in-news-outperforms-other-environments-marketers-say) those in other kinds of online content, DV research shows, and news attracts wealthier, more educated and more


[engaged](https://doubleverify.com/blog/web/verify/consumers-value-brands-that-support-the-creation-of-news) consumers. With its relatively lower CPMs and CPCs, news can help advertisers reach their business goals


[more efficiently](https://doubleverify.com/company/newsroom/news-helps-advertisers-get-more-from-their-media-investment-new-analysis-finds) .


Publishers say these findings are sparking constructive conversations with advertisers and agencies, and they’re encouraged by the progress. And budgets have shifted, but not yet in proportion to the positive sentiment. The good news: Publishers believe the views of senior leaders are slowly trickling down to the hands-on-keyboards teams that make day-to-day buying decisions.


## 2. AI Slop Has a Surprising Upside


AI is an existential threat to news. With chatbots now providing search query summaries, consumers may find it less necessary to click through to news sites. Publishers are increasingly looking to video and audio content to help offset potential traffic disruption (although, depending on the topic, monetizing this content can be just as challenging as monetizing news).


At the same time, publishers see a growing opportunity in the


[proliferation](https://doubleverify.com/blog/web/verify/dv-exclusive-inside-an-ai-slop-factory) of low-quality AI-generated content and fraud: News remains a trusted, quality environment, a distinction they intend to make increasingly clear to advertisers.


## 3. Nuanced Brand Suitability Avoidance Is a Valuable Skill. Let’s Teach It.


Brand suitability settings can and should be tailored to specific goals and contexts. But too often, publishers say, media buyers apply the same settings for all clients and campaigns. This overly broad, one-size-fits-all approach can limit campaign reach and performance by unnecessarily avoiding content that, when looked at more closely, is perfectly suitable.


The same goes for keyword-based tools: A blanket avoidance of the word “shot,” for example, meant to filter out violent news, would also flag “basketball shot.” Publishers tell us they’re increasingly pushing back on the use of these tools.


The solution? Team education. Senior leaders who understand the benefit of more nuanced, category-based suitability settings, please ensure your junior staffers are equipped to execute them.


## 4. Buying News Is Getting Easier


Publishers note a perception among media buyers that news campaigns take more time and effort to manage than non-news campaigns. As a result, stretched teams often gravitate toward options they view as simpler and less time-consuming. (For their part, publishers also say unnecessary back-and-forth on suitability settings eats into their own margins.)


They’re responding in practical ways. Some are testing discounted pricing or other incentives for advertisers who use simpler campaign settings. Others are


[making the case](https://doubleverify.com/blog/web/publisher/advertising-in-news-outperforms-other-environments-marketers-say) that the campaign efficiency and performance gains news provides are well worth any additional operational overhead.


## 5. Advertiser Champions: You Make a Real Difference


Publishers agree: Advertisers who share their experiences and successes working with news content send a powerful signal to the market and help build confidence in news. Proof points and business outcomes carry even more weight than sentiment alone.


Brand support of news matters to consumers as well. In a DV


[survey](https://doubleverify.com/blog/web/verify/consumers-value-brands-that-support-the-creation-of-news) , 51% of consumers with a household income of $100K or more, and 42% of consumers overall, said they actively value brands that support the creation of news by advertising alongside it.


## DV’s Ongoing Commitment to News Publishers


The conversations in New York and London underscored the value of close, ongoing dialogue with publishers, and we're grateful to everyone who shared their perspectives so openly. Supporting news is a long-term commitment at DV, and the News Accelerator is how we deliver on it: through close collaboration with publishers, product innovation and ongoing research and education.


Feedback from publishers informs our priorities on an ongoing basis, and we'll keep sharing what we hear along the way.


## Next Steps


If you're a news publisher and would like to contribute your perspective or join the DV News Accelerator Publisher Network, we'd love to hear from you.
